title: Boundary enforcement uses CI path checks and CODEOWNERS
context: Alternative approaches: runtime permission checks only; honor-system enforcement; per-file access control.
decision: CI enforces the architectural boundary using: (1) `cargo-deny` gates Rust dependencies against the library registry; (2) `dependency-cruiser` gates TypeScript imports across package boundaries; (3) a path-scope check blocks pulls that write `runs/` and `nodes/` together (except the lifecycle pair); (4) CODEOWNERS assigns semantic files to the repository owner and leaves runs/ and layout/ unowned.
consequences: Enforcement happens at merge time, not runtime; violations are caught in CI; the boundary is organizational (via CODEOWNERS) and technical (via path checks); agents can write to `runs/` and `layout/` without approval; wave 10 writes the CODEOWNERS file.
